1	//! Cross-provider conformance suite for the `Model::invoke` stream
2	//! event-ordering contract.
3	//!
4	//! This internal (never-published) crate hosts a provider-agnostic checker and
5	//! a paced HTTP server. Each subject in `tests/conformance.rs` serves its own
6	//! captured wire bytes through that server and hands back the stream from its
7	//! real `Model::invoke`, so the suite exercises the production driver and the
8	//! production translator together — not a reimplementation of either.
9	//!
10	//! See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-sma-533-stream-conformance-design.md`.
11	#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
12	
13	mod check;
14	mod declines;
15	pub mod eventstream;
16	#[cfg(test)]
17	mod fakes;
18	mod server;
19	
20	pub use check::classify;
21	pub use declines::DECLINED;
22	pub use server::{Ending, PacedServer, Script};
23	
24	use std::time::Duration;
25	
26	use futures_util::stream::{BoxStream, StreamExt};
27	use paigasus_helikon_core::{CancellationToken, FinishReason, ModelError, ModelEvent};
28	
29	/// One wire script, run against every subject that can express it.
30	///
31	/// The `a`/`b` pairs differ only in whether the script lets the translator
32	/// observe a stop reason before the stream ends. That distinction is the whole
33	/// point: with no stop reason buffered there is nothing for a broken driver to
34	/// wrongly flush, so the `a` variants cannot fail assertions 5 and 6 on their
35	/// own.
36	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
37	pub enum Scenario {
38	    /// Deltas, stop reason, usage, terminator, clean EOF.
39	    CleanStop,
40	    /// Stop reason observed, then the body ends cleanly with no terminator.
41	    TruncatedAfterStopReason,
42	    /// Body ends cleanly mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
43	    TruncatedMidGeneration,
44	    /// Body aborted mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
45	    ErrorMidGeneration,
46	    /// Stop reason observed, then the body is aborted.
47	    ErrorAfterStopReason,
48	    /// Cancelled mid-generation; no stop reason is ever observed.
49	    CancelMidGeneration,
50	    /// Stop reason observed, then cancelled before end-of-stream.
51	    CancelAfterStopReason,
52	    /// A tool call whose name arrives split across two or more deltas.
53	    FragmentedToolName,
54	    /// One complete tool call followed by a tool-use stop reason.
55	    ToolCallCleanStop,
56	}
57	
58	impl Scenario {
59	    /// Every scenario, in table order.
60	    pub const ALL: &'static [Scenario] = &[
61	        Scenario::CleanStop,
62	        Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason,
63	        Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration,
64	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration,
65	        Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,
66	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration,
67	        Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason,
68	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName,
69	        Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
70	    ];
71	
72	    /// Whether this scenario's script must let the translator observe a stop
73	    /// reason. Cross-checked against each subject's own declaration so a
74	    /// mis-transcribed fixture cannot make assertion 3 pass vacuously.
75	    pub fn expects_stop_reason(self) -> bool {
76	        matches!(
77	            self,
78	            Scenario::CleanStop
79	                | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
80	                | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
81	                | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
82	                | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
83	        )
84	    }
85	}
86	
87	/// A contract violation, classified. Ordering matters — see `classify`.
88	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
89	pub enum Violation {
90	    /// More than one `Finish` was emitted (assertion 1).
91	    DuplicateFinish,
92	    /// A `Usage` was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 2).
93	    UsageAfterFinish,
94	    /// Any other event, or an `Err`, was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 1).
95	    EventAfterFinish,
96	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason emitted no `Finish`
97	    /// (assertion 3).
98	    MissingFinish,
99	    /// A `Finish` was emitted although no stop reason was observed
100	    /// (assertion 4).
101	    FinishOnTruncation,
102	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after cancellation (assertion 5).
103	    FinishOnCancel,
104	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
105	    FinishAfterError,
106	    /// A `call_id` carried a number of name-bearing deltas other than one, or
107	    /// the name did not match the fixture's declared tool name (assertion 7).
108	    ToolNameNotExactlyOnce {
109	        /// The call whose name emission was wrong.
110	        call_id: String,
111	        /// How many deltas for that `call_id` carried `Some(name)`.
112	        count: usize,
113	    },
114	    /// A `ProviderData` event named a `call_id` for which the stream carried no
115	    /// `ToolCallDelta` (assertion 8).
116	    ProviderDataUnknownCall {
117	        /// The `call_id` that no streamed tool call used.
118	        call_id: String,
119	    },
120	    /// The stream did not produce the minimum evidence its scenario requires,
121	    /// so the assertions would have passed vacuously.
122	    InsufficientEvidence(&'static str),
123	    /// The terminal event carried a different `FinishReason` than the
124	    /// subject's fixture declares, so the bytes served are not the ones the
125	    /// scenario describes (spec §7.1).
126	    FinishReasonMismatch {
127	        /// What the subject's `fixture_finish_reason` declared.
128	        expected: FinishReason,
129	        /// What the stream actually emitted.
130	        observed: FinishReason,
131	    },
132	    /// The stream did not terminate within the per-scenario timeout.
133	    Timeout,
134	    /// The subject's `encodes_stop_reason` disagreed with the scenario's own
135	    /// expectation, so its fixture does not match the script it claims.
136	    StopReasonDeclarationMismatch {
137	        /// What the scenario requires.
138	        expected: bool,
139	        /// What the subject declared.
140	        declared: bool,

1	//! The registered conformance subjects.
2	//!
3	//! Each subject in this file serves its own wire bytes through the crate's
4	//! paced HTTP server and hands back the stream from its real `Model::invoke`,
5	//! so every assertion in `assert_conforms` is made about production driver and
6	//! production translator code — never about a reimplementation of either.
7	//!
8	//! ## Adding a subject
9	//!
10	//! One `mod <subject> { … }` per subject, holding its fixture helpers, its
11	//! `StreamUnderTest` impl and one `#[tokio::test]` that calls
12	//! `assert_conforms`. The module scoping is not cosmetic: it is what lets every
13	//! subject call its helpers `text_delta`, `script`, `request` and so on without
14	//! a per-subject prefix, and it keeps six subjects' worth of near-identical
15	//! names from colliding in one flat namespace.
16	//!
17	//! Two rules apply to every subject, and both exist because breaking them makes
18	//! a check pass without measuring anything:
19	//!
20	//! 1. **Decline reasons are literal strings**, copied by hand from
21	//!    `src/declines.rs`. A subject that looked its reasons up from `DECLINED`
22	//!    would satisfy that table's two-directional cross-check by construction,
23	//!    which is exactly the drift the table exists to catch.
24	//! 2. **`encodes_stop_reason` is measured from the bytes about to be served**,
25	//!    never restated from `Scenario::expects_stop_reason`. Restating it
26	//!    compares the harness's expectation with itself. See the Bedrock impl for
27	//!    what it catches.
28	
29	use paigasus_helikon_core::{
30	    CancellationToken, ContentPart, FinishReason, Item, Model, ModelRequest, ToolDef,
31	};
32	use paigasus_helikon_provider_stream_conformance::{
33	    assert_conforms, eventstream::frame, Ending, Outcome, PacedServer, Scenario, Script,
34	    StreamUnderTest,
35	};
36	use serde_json::json;
37	
38	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the Bedrock
39	/// `ConverseStream` provider.
40	///
41	/// # Fixture provenance
42	///
43	/// Bedrock is the one subject in this suite whose wire format is binary, and
44	/// the repo holds no captured Bedrock traffic to transcribe. So — as the task
45	/// brief directs when no capture exists — every event shape here is derived
46	/// from two sources inside the workspace, and from nothing else:
47	///
48	/// 1. **The translator's own match arms**, `providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`.
49	///    Which `ConverseStreamOutput` variants matter, and what each one must
50	///    carry to produce a `ModelEvent`, is read off the arms that consume them:
51	///    `ContentBlockDelta`/`Text` to `TokenDelta`, `ContentBlockStart`/`ToolUse`
52	///    plus `ContentBlockDelta`/`ToolUse` to `ToolCallDelta`, `MessageStop` to
53	///    the buffered stop reason, `Metadata`/`usage` to `Usage` then `Finish`.
54	/// 2. **The vendored AWS Converse types** in `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` 1.140.0.
55	///    Every JSON key below is the key that crate's own deserializer reads, and
56	///    every `:event-type` is the union member name its
57	///    `ConverseStreamOutputUnmarshaller` dispatches on
58	///    (`src/event_stream_serde.rs`). Per-shape references sit on each helper.
59	///
60	/// Nothing here is transcribed from vendor documentation, and no shape is
61	/// invented: a frame the SDK's decoder does not recognise is dropped silently
62	/// by the translator's forward-compat catch-all rather than rejected, so an
63	/// invented shape would present as a translator bug and not as a bad fixture.
64	///
65	/// # Why there are no `.bin` fixture files
66	///
67	/// A `vnd.amazon.eventstream` frame is a length-prefixed header block wrapped
68	/// in two CRC-32s, so a checked-in `.bin` would be neither reviewable nor
69	/// editable, and any byte edited by hand would fail its CRC rather than test
70	/// anything. `eventstream::frame` exists precisely to avoid that: it encodes
71	/// each fixture with the same encoder the SDK itself uses, so the bytes that
72	/// reach the wire are real while the fixture stays readable as JSON.
73	mod bedrock {
74	    use super::*;
75	
76	    /// The tool name every Bedrock tool fixture declares.
77	    const TOOL_NAME: &str = "get_weather";
78	
79	    /// `toolUseId` for the single tool call in the tool fixtures.
80	    ///
81	    /// Deliberately *not* claimed to match any real Bedrock id format: the SDK
82	    /// types this field as a plain `String` with no format constraint
83	    /// (`_tool_use_block_start.rs`: `pub tool_use_id: String`), and the
84	    /// translator copies it verbatim into `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta.call_id`
85	    /// (`stream.rs:116`), so nothing under test inspects its shape. The value
86	    /// is fixed and self-describing purely so failure output is stable and
87	    /// greppable.
88	    const TOOL_USE_ID: &str = "tooluse_conformance_0";
89	
90	    /// The `:event-type` value carried by the one event that encodes a stop
91	    /// reason. Used by [`Bedrock::encodes_stop_reason`] to measure a script.
92	    const MESSAGE_STOP_EVENT_TYPE: &str = "messageStop";
93	
94	    /// `messageStart`, which opens every Converse stream.
95	    ///
96	    /// The translator ignores it (`ConverseStreamOutput::MessageStart(_) => {}`);
97	    /// it is here because a real stream always sends it first, and a fixture
98	    /// that silently omitted the opening event would not be the stream it
99	    /// claims to be. Key: `role` (`shape_message_start_event.rs`), value from
100	    /// `ConversationRole` (`_conversation_role.rs`: `"assistant"`).
101	    fn message_start() -> Vec<u8> {
102	        frame("messageStart", &json!({ "role": "assistant" }))
103	    }
104	
105	    /// One text delta. `stream.rs`'s `ContentBlockDelta::Text` arm turns this
106	    /// into `ModelEvent::TokenDelta`.
107	    ///
108	    /// Keys: `contentBlockIndex` and `delta`
109	    /// (`shape_content_block_delta_event.rs`), with `text` the
110	    /// `ContentBlockDelta` union member (`shape_content_block_delta.rs`).
111	    fn text_delta(text: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
112	        frame(
113	            "contentBlockDelta",

2193	/// the two scenarios while leaving the other green — see the task report for

21	## Conventional Commits
22	
23	Every commit message **and** every PR title must conform to
24	[Conventional Commits 1.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/),
25	with the type and scope constrained as below. Three layers enforce
26	this:
27	
28	| Layer | Fires when | Bypass |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| Local `commit-msg` hook | `git commit` | `git commit --no-verify` |
31	| `ci / commits` job | PR open + sync | none — fix the message |
32	| `pr-title / pr-title` job | PR open/edit/sync | none — fix the title |
33	
34	### Allowed types and semver effect
35

## Conventional Commits

Every commit message **and** every PR title must conform to
[Conventional Commits 1.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/),
with the type and scope constrained as below. Three layers enforce
this:

| Layer | Fires when | Bypass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local `commit-msg` hook | `git commit` | `git commit --no-verify` |
| `ci / commits` job | PR open + sync | none — fix the message |
| `pr-title / pr-title` job | PR open/edit/sync | none — fix the title |

### Allowed types and semver effect

This project is currently pre-1.0 (`0.x.y` across every crate);
release-plz applies its own pre-1.0 bump rules — consult the
[release-plz docs](https://release-plz.dev/docs) for the exact
mapping in effect today. The table below shows the **post-1.0**
mapping that becomes operative after the first `1.0.0` release:

| Type | Semver effect (post-1.0) | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feat` | minor | New user-visible capability |
| `fix` | patch | Bug fix |
| `feat!` or any type with `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer | major | API break |
| `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `perf`, `style`, `build`, `ci`, `revert` | none | Everything else |

### Scope allowlist

Scope is optional. If present, must match one of:

- **Crate scopes** (one per workspace member, facade collapsed to `facade`):
  `core`, `cli`, `facade`, `macros`, `mcp`, `tools`, `evals`,
  `providers`, `providers-openai`, `providers-anthropic`,
  `runtime`, `runtime-tokio`, `runtime-axum`, `runtime-temporal`, `runtime-agentcore`,
  `runtime-actix`
- **Cross-cutting scopes:** `workspace`, `workflows`, `ci`, `deps`,
  `release`, `repo`, `docs`, `contributing`, `readme`, `claude`,
  `spec`, `specs`, `plan`, `lints`

Canonical source is [`.versionrc`](./.versionrc). The
`pr-title.yml` workflow mirrors the same list — they must change
together.

### Examples

Valid:

```text
feat(core): SMA-304 add Model trait
fix(providers-openai): SMA-312 handle 429 retry-after header
chore(deps): bump tokio from 1.40 to 1.41
docs(contributing): SMA-310 document supply-chain section
ci(workflows): SMA-306 add cargo-audit workflow

```

Invalid:

```text
wip                                  # no type

Update README                        # wrong format; PR title would also fail subjectPattern
feat(unknown-scope): SMA-### foo     # scope not in allowlist
feat(core): Add Model trait          # PR title would fail subjectPattern (uppercase start)
```

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
Approach A is sound, and I found no test that depends on `[DONE]`. In async-openai 0.43.0, `[DONE]` and body EOF end the Responses stream the same way, for every terminal event. But the spec is about to write a "complete" edit list into a CAPTURED header that probably still has an edit nobody recorded. The new CONTRIBUTING rule also cannot express that kind of edit, and it does not address the root cause of the four hand-authored files.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **The "Added: nothing" edit list is probably incomplete: `responses_tool_call.txt` appears to have its keys reordered to match its siblings** - The header calls the file "a literal transcription" (`responses_tool_call.txt:29`). Design step 1 keeps the three trims as the full Removed list and adds "Added: nothing". But the key order in the file is not the order of the byte-faithful capture of the same endpoint and model, taken two days later:
  - Delta event, fixture line 81: `"type","sequence_number","item_id","output_index","delta"`.
  - Delta event, `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt:69` (byte-faithful): `"type","delta","item_id","obfuscation","output_index","sequence_number"`. This is `type` first, then alphabetical.
  - The same difference occurs in `output_item.added` (lines 78 vs 66), `output_item.done` and `response.completed`. The fixture's `response` object order is `id,object,created_at,model,output,status,incomplete_details,usage` (line 102). That is the hand-authored sibling layout (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt:5`), not the wire order at `zero_args:78`.
  - This points to a transcription that was shaped to look like its siblings. `[DONE]` is one result of that, and the key order is a second.
  - Caveat: the SMA-562 spec, line 88, quotes a resumed-stream item in yet another key order. So the wire order may vary by code path, or that quote was reformatted. That makes this a strong inference, not a proof.
  | Why it matters: The ticket exists to make a CAPTURED label truthful. The new CONTRIBUTING rule says a CAPTURED header "lists every edit". The flagship fixture would break that rule on the day it lands. | Suggested fix: Before you write the header, diff the fixture's key order against the 2026-11-21 `get_weather` capture (same request shape, same model). If they differ, record the reorder as an edit, remove the word "literal", and give the edit structure a third part (see the MAJOR finding on the CONTRIBUTING rule). Also correct the root-cause sentence in Intent ("no place for additions"). The cause is wider: the transcription was conformed to the sibling files.

### MAJOR
- **The spec repeats the evidence gap that caused this ticket** - Evidence says "No raw copy of the 2026-08-20 capture exists ... cannot be proven". Then lines 42-43 decide not to commit the 2026-11-21 captures, and give only a summary table. The SMA-562 spec (§9, lines 490-497) did the same, which is why nobody can check 2026-08-20 today. The SMA-522 spec has precedent for doing better: "Appendix A — captured traces" (line 439). | Why it matters: The next auditor cannot verify "None contains the string DONE", and cannot settle the BLOCKER. | Suggested fix: Add an appendix to this spec. For each of the four captures, include the redacted response headers, the last event verbatim, the trailing bytes (for example `...}\n\n<EOF>`), and the curl exit status. For the tool capture, also include every event envelope, so that the key order is on record. Redact org, project and request ids.

- **The CONTRIBUTING rule is incomplete** - It has five gaps:
  - (a) Removed/Added cannot express an in-place change. Examples: a key reorder (the BLOCKER), and "response id shortened" (`chat_text_usage_trailing.txt:4`).
  - (b) CAPTURED or HAND-AUTHORED is binary. `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt:1-7` is part captured and part reconstructed.
  - (c) The rule gives HAND-AUTHORED files no rule of their own. But four of the five defective files are HAND-AUTHORED. Their defect was framing copied from a different endpoint (Chat Completions). "Do not add a line that the wire did not send" means nothing for a file that no wire sent.
  - (d) No scope for formats without comment syntax. The JSON fixtures in `crates/paigasus-helikon-tools/tests/fixtures/` cannot carry a `:` header.
  - (e) Inline wire bytes in test code are not covered. `responses_wire.rs` `sse()` and the conformance helpers carried the same `[DONE]` assumption.
  | Why it matters: The rule is the only thing that stops this from happening again, and it does not cover the failure that actually occurred. | Suggested fix:
  - Use three parts: Removed / Added / Changed (reorder, reformat, value edits). Write "nothing" where a part is empty.
  - Allow a mixed label, for example "CAPTURED, with reconstructed parts: ...".
  - For HAND-AUTHORED: "name the source of each shape (a capture or a vendored type). Never copy framing from a different endpoint or API."
  - Add a scope line. SSE/text fixtures carry a `:` header. Other formats record provenance in the doc comment of the test that loads them. Inline wire helpers cite their source the same way.

- **The hand-authored header overstates the evidence for two files** - Design step 2 puts "as the 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-21 captures show" in all four headers. No capture of `response.failed` or of a content-filter `response.incomplete` exists. The spec itself says these cannot be triggered (Approach B). The captures cover only `response.completed` and `response.incomplete` with `max_output_tokens`. | Why it matters: This is the same class of overclaim that the ticket removes. | Suggested fix: Write the header per file. For `responses_failed.txt` and `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`, write: "no capture of this terminal event exists; `[DONE]` is omitted because no captured Responses stream ends with it."

- **No test will cover a trailing `[DONE]` after this change, and Goal 1 forbids the remedy** - `builder.rs:72` advertises `base_url` for "LiteLLM, vLLM, Azure-via-proxy". After the change, no Responses test sends `[DONE]`. Today, tolerance comes from the generic `post_stream` path in async-openai (`client.rs:860`, `break` on `[DONE]`). The Gemini and LiteLLM drivers in this repo have their own `[DONE]` arms. If the Responses backend ever moves off async-openai's stream, a compatible server that sends `[DONE]` could cause an `Err` after `Finish`, and no test would fail. I did not verify whether any compatible server sends `[DONE]` on `/responses`. | Why it matters: This is a silent loss of coverage for a use case that the crate advertises. | Suggested fix: Change Goal 1 to "no fixture presents `[DONE]` as OpenAI wire behaviour". Add one clearly labelled test in `responses_wire.rs`, for example `trailing_done_sentinel_is_tolerated`. Document it as a compatibility check, not a wire claim. The Gemini subject's labelled synthetic `done()` (`conformance.rs:2409-2426`) is the precedent.

### MINOR
- **The spec miscounts the uses of `done()`** - It says "its two uses (`CleanStop`, `ToolCallCleanStop`)". There are three: `conformance.rs:3046`, `:3112` and `:3266`. The third is the `("[DONE]", done())` row in `scan_finds_only_the_terminal_event`. If you delete the function, that row fails to compile. Also, the quoted phrase "the stream terminator every committed fixture ... ends with" is the doc comment on `done()` itself (`:2946-2947`), not the module doc. | Suggested fix: List all three uses, and say to delete the scan row.

- **Goal 4 misses some stale cross-references** -
  - `conformance.rs:2890-2893` says "four of the five `responses_*.txt`". There are six.
  - `responses_tool_call.txt:25-26` says "`event:` lines are kept, unlike this directory's other `responses_*.txt`". The zero-args file keeps them too.
  - `zero_args:48-50` says "Unlike every sibling fixture here, this file does NOT end with `data: [DONE]`". This becomes false. Step 4 names only lines 56-58.
  - `conformance.rs:2806-2811` grounds the text shapes on a file that will now be labelled HAND-AUTHORED, and should say so.
  - Goal 4 read literally also covers dated design artifacts: SMA-562 spec:419 (`responses_tool_call.txt:104`), and SMA-562 plan:655 and :988 ("line 99").
  | Suggested fix: Add these items to the list, and exempt `docs/superpowers/**` explicitly.

- **Line-number citations will go stale again** - Every header edit moves the numbers at 2954, 2974, 2989 and 3004. Each CAPTURED event has a unique `sequence_number` (2, 3-7, 8, 9, 10). | Suggested fix: Cite by `sequence_number`, not by line. The verification step "each citation points to its event" then becomes stable.

- **Nothing enforces Goal 1 after merge** - `[DONE]` and EOF give identical `ModelEvent`s, so no behaviour test can detect a sentinel that someone adds back. The new correction note will contain the literal text `data: [DONE]`. If one header line loses its leading `:`, that line becomes a real data line (eventsource-stream `parser.rs:97-109`). | Suggested fix: Add a test in `responses_streaming.rs` that asserts no `responses_*.txt` has a line equal to `data: [DONE]`. Alternatively, write the correction note without that literal text.

- **The doc for the Responses `CleanStop` should name the terminator** - `lib.rs:38-41` defines CleanStop as "..., terminator, clean EOF" and TruncatedAfterStopReason as "no terminator". Without `[DONE]`, a reviewer can think CleanStop now carries the declined TruncatedAfterStopReason bytes. | Suggested fix: In the arm comment, say that `response.completed` is both the stop reason and the terminator, and that the wire has no separate sentinel. The decline string does not change.

- **The rollout is not stated** - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/Cargo.toml` has no `include`/`exclude`, so `tests/fixtures/*.txt` are in the published package. release-plz will patch-bump providers-openai (0.4.1 to 0.4.2) and cascade to the facade, for a test-only change. | Suggested fix: Say this in the spec, and choose the commit scopes: `test(providers-openai)` and `docs(contributing)`. No scope exists for the conformance crate.

- **The evidence under-claims in one place and over-claims in another** - The equivalence of `[DONE]` and EOF is proven by code for every terminal event, not only by the one shape that SMA-562 probed:
  - async-openai 0.43.0 `client.rs:846-873`: `[DONE]` gives `break` and EOF ends the loop. Both drop `tx`.
  - `responses.rs:71` returns on `None`.
  - `responses.rs:695-702`: `response.failed` gives `Err`, and the driver returns before it reads anything more.
  Cite this code. In the other direction, "Chat Completions does send `[DONE]`" has no first-party capture in the repo. `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt` is a LiteLLM proxy capture, and the `empty_choices` variant is HAND-AUTHORED. Soften the sentence or cite a source.

- **CLAUDE.md has no pointer to the rule** - Agents write most fixtures, and they read CLAUDE.md first ("Fixture line endings"). | Suggested fix: Add a one-line pointer to the new CONTRIBUTING section. This is a pointer, not a second copy.

### QUESTIONS
- Did each 2026-11-21 `curl` exit 0 because the server closed the stream? Or did `--max-time` or Ctrl-C stop it? A truncated capture also contains no `DONE`.
- Is the key order of the 2026-11-21 tool capture the same as the fixture, or the same as the zero-args capture? The answer settles the BLOCKER.
- The rule "applies from now on", and on merge day several files do not follow it: the LiteLLM CAPTURED fixtures (`tool_call_stream.txt:1-9` lists no edits) and the mixed `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`. Will you file a Linear follow-up for them?
- Does the CONTRIBUTING rule cover inline scripts in `conformance.rs`? Is a labelled synthetic addition allowed there, as in the Gemini `done()`?

## What's good
- The scope is correct. I checked the whole repo. The only `[DONE]` senders on a `/responses` mock are the five fixtures, `responses_wire.rs:54` and the `openai_responses` `done()`. `cancellation.rs` and `chat_wire.rs` use Chat only. The citations 78, 81-93, 96 and 99 are correct today. The only consumer of the four hand-authored files is `responses_streaming.rs` `run()` (wiremock `set_body_raw`). The conformance suite loads no fixture files.
- The `:` header is safe. eventsource-stream 0.2.3 ignores comment lines (`event_stream.rs:70`). A blank line after the header dispatches nothing, because the data buffer is empty (`:100-102`). `responses_tool_call.txt` already starts with `:` at byte 0 and passes, and the chat fixtures put a header directly before `data:` with no blank line.
- The change improves fidelity. Today, no Responses conformance scenario covers the real production ending (EOF after `response.completed`). After this change, `CleanStop` and `ToolCallCleanStop` cover it. The anti-goal "if behaviour changes, stop and investigate" is the right tripwire.

## What's good
- The scope is correct. I checked the whole repo. The only `[DONE]` senders on a `/responses` mock are the five fixtures, `responses_wire.rs:54` and the `openai_responses` `done()`. `cancellation.rs` and `chat_wire.rs` use Chat only. - The `:` header is safe. eventsource-stream 0.2.3 ignores comment lines (`event_stream.rs:70`). A blank line after the header dispatches nothing, because the data buffer is empty (`:100-102`). `responses_tool_call.txt` already starts with `:` at byte 0 and passes, and the chat fixtures put a header directly before `data:` with no blank line.
- The change improves fidelity. Today, no Responses conformance scenario covers the real production ending (EOF after `response.completed`). After this change, `CleanStop` and `ToolCallCleanStop` cover it. The anti-goal "if behaviour changes, stop and investigate" is the right tripwire.
